html:
The Vienna Circle was a group of philosophers, scientists and mathematicians who met in Vienna from 1924 to 1936 around the philosopher Moritz Schlick.

Members such as Rudolf Carnap and Otto Neurath held that only statements that can be checked by experience or are true by logic have meaning, a view called logical positivism. They took ideas from Ludwig Wittgenstein's Tractatus and wanted philosophy to serve science. The logician Kurt Gödel attended, and Karl Popper argued with them.

Schlick was shot dead by a former student in 1936. Most members were Jewish or on the left and fled after the Anschluss, many to America and Britain, where their ideas shaped philosophy after the war. It was part of the remarkable culture of Vienna that also produced Freud and Klimt. See Austria.
sum: The Vienna Circle was a group of philosophers, scientists and mathematicians who met in Vienna from 1924 to 1936 around the philosopher Moritz Schlick.
